subject: Sandbox evaluation credits, packaging options, and runtime guardrails for Optimize toolkit
messages:
From: Tim Owens <tim.owens@atlasgrid.com>

Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-22T09:15:00-04:00
Subject: Sizing & credits question for Optimize toolkit pilot

Jasmine —

Thanks for the demo yesterday. A couple of follow-ups from our infra and finance teams as we scope a 6‑week pilot:

- Can you outline how sandbox/testbench credits would apply to batching vs KV/prefix cache usage? Our initial workload is heavy on short context lookups (~45 tokens) with lots of repeated prefixes.
- Any recommended quantization profiles you suggest for a production-feel evaluation (latency vs quality tradeoffs)? We are open to INT8 if quality is acceptable.
- We want one clear pricing scenario: rough monthly TCO for 200M tokens (mostly gen) with and without NV cache hits (50% vs 90%).

Also, curious whether Redwood can provide a small set of synthetic traffic scripts or a test harness we can run in our sandbox — that will speed up internal sign-off. Attaching a short outline of what our team will test.

Thanks,
Tim

Head of Platform
AtlasGrid

Subject: Re: Sizing & credits question for Optimize toolkit pilot

Hi Tim —

Appreciate the clear list. High level answers below; I included Karthik and Lauren for technical and commercial follow-up respectively.

Quick summary (will put a short MAP together after you confirm scope):
- Sandbox/testbench credits: we can provide up to 200k inference credit units for a 6‑week evaluation (applies to token usage and is consumed by generation + embedding calls). We treat cache-prefetch and KV hits as reducing billed tokens on Redwood-hosted runtime when the cache is served server-side. For a dedicated sandbox we can enable an instrumented KV-cache so you can see hit-rate breakdown by prefix.
- Credit attribution: credits are deducted on a post-aggregation basis; i.e., if a request is served entirely from the KV cache (100% hit), token consumption recorded to the runtime is reduced per our billing model — we’ll include worked examples in the MAP.
- Quantization recommendation: start with 8-bit (INT8) for the Optimize toolkit profiles — it’s the best first step for AtlasGrid to test. If you want more aggressive savings, we can demo 4-bit (Q4) on non-critical endpoints but expect a small quality delta on long-context synthesis. Karthik: see the attached quick profiles and a recommended runbook.
- Pricing scenarios (very rough):
  * Base (no cache): ~$0.18 / 1k tokens -> monthly ~$36,000 for 200M tokens
  * With 50% effective cache hit: effective billed tokens drop by ~40% (prefetch amortization) -> ~$21,600
  * With 90% hit (optimistic): billed tokens drop by ~80% -> ~$7,200
We will provide more precise model once you share a short sample of token distribution (gen vs embeddings vs short prefix hits).

Test harness: we have a small traffic generator and a canonical set of prompts we can share. We'll provide containerized scripts that emit realistic prefix-skewed traffic and a trace file so you can reproduce our KV cache hit assumptions.

Next steps / asks:
- Tim: can you confirm a target model family (e.g., Llama-2 derivative, MPT-family) and a representative token distribution CSV?
- Lauren: can you draft a short MAP (mutual action plan) with the sandbox credit line and target acceptance criteria?
- Karthik: can you add recommended quant profiles for the two model families Tim might pick and a latency delta table?

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30m call if you want to run numbers together.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Sizing & credits question for Optimize toolkit pilot — technical notes

Tim / Jasmine —

Quick technical notes to supplement Jasmine's reply. I kept this high level so your infra folks can rapidly prototype with our scripts.

Quantization profiles (starting point):
- Profile A (safer): INT8 (per-channel symmetric) for decoder-only workloads. Quality delta vs fp16: ~1–2% measured on common semantic tasks, latency ~15–25% lower.
- Profile B (aggressive): Q4 (4-bit) for non-critical batch jobs; expect occasional decoding glitches on long, open-ended prompts — latency ~35–50% lower vs fp16.

KV cache and billing assumptions:
- Effective billed token reduction is a function of cache hit rate and prefix prefetch strategy. A 50% hit can often translate to ~35–45% token billing reduction (we model prefetch overhead in our MAP).
- Our test harness will instrument hit/miss traces, per-request latency, and token delta so you can feed actuals back into your finance model.

Batching guidance for pilot:
- Target micro-batch latency SLO: 120–180ms P95 for request sizes <= 64 tokens. Use a max batch window of 15ms for low-latency routes; increase to 50–75ms for throughput-oriented paths.
- For your prefix-heavy workload, recommend a hybrid route: small-latency routing for unknown prefixes, cache-first routing for known prefixes with a slightly higher batch window to improve kernel utilization.

Examples we will include in the MAP:
- 200M monthly tokens, Model: optimize-std-1 (fp16) -> baseline numbers (Jasmine's draft)
- INT8 variant -> expected cost delta: ~30–40% savings, quality delta: small on short-form generation
- Q4 variant -> ~55–65% savings with careful scope (batch-only endpoints)

Deliverables I will upload to the shared Drive after this note:
- quant_profiles.csv (simple profile list + recommended use cases)
- a ready-to-run container with the traffic generator and an example config for AtlasGrid

If this looks good I can join your infra sync tomorrow to walk through the runbook and run a quick smoke test with the sandbox credits.

-Karthik
